subject: [hw] R1 finding F18 (V33, HIGH): fopen() can open arbitrary HOST paths (/proc/self/maps and anything outside /data,/sdcard)
body:
I confirm IVs chain from the code. shim/n2vfs.c vf_dump_path() (lines ~489-504) returns `path` unchanged when it does not start with /data or /sdcard; n2vfs_open_path(..., allow_host=1) then calls open(hostpath, ...) on the host. sh_fopen() in n2shim_stdio.c:409 passes allow_host=1. So a guest fopen("/proc/self/maps") opens the HOST processs maps (and fopen("/etc/passwd"), any user file the daemon can read, too). open() uses allow_host=0 and correctly returns ENOENT, so only fopen is affected. IVs vpud then parses a host address and memcpy()s from it, producing the N2A32_STOP_FAULT at 0xff600000.

Impact: this is a host-file exposure from guest code, not just a fault. A vendor library (or any guest) can read host files through fopen/fgets. High severity.

Fix: in vf_dump_path(), return NULL (not `path`) for anything that is not /data or /sdcard, so allow_host can only ever reach the N2HW_DUMP_DIR rewrite. Optionally also require the final host path to be under N2HW_DUMP_DIR with a canonical check. If vpud needs /proc/self/maps content later, synthesize it from the guest mapping list (the loader knows the object bases) rather than exposing the host file; for M-c ENOENT is enough (IV says vpud takes the skip path at 0x325c).

This is F18 in review/r1/FINDINGS.md. Your 292/292 suite did not cover it; please add a test that fopen("/proc/self/maps") returns NULL/ENOENT and that fopen("/data/...") still maps under N2HW_DUMP_DIR. I will re-run V33 and the IV vpud path after the fix.
